name: Components
heading: Components
description: Free CSS-only Tailwind CSS components with WCAG AA/AAA accessibility built in. No JavaScript required, framework-agnostic, and compatible with Django, HTMX, Laravel, React, Vue, and any stack. Ready to use and easy to customize.
metaTitle: CSS-Only Tailwind CSS Components Library | Frutjam
metaDescription: Free CSS-only Tailwind CSS components. WCAG accessible, no JavaScript, framework-agnostic. Works with Django, HTMX, Laravel, React, and any stack.

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — the vast majority of components are pure CSS with zero JavaScript. Buttons, badges, cards, forms, alerts, modals, drawers, tabs, and more all work with plain HTML and CSS. A small number of components that have no native HTML equivalent (toast positioning, combobox filtering, carousel controls) offer optional lightweight JS helpers, but the CSS layout and styling requires no JavaScript at all.

mainEntity.name: Do Frutjam components work with Django, HTMX, and Laravel?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — Frutjam is framework-agnostic. Because every component is CSS-only, it works with any server-rendered stack. Django templates, HTMX, Laravel Blade, Rails ERB, plain HTML — if you can output HTML, Frutjam works. No React, no build pipeline, no JavaScript framework required.

Yes — WCAG AA contrast is guaranteed on every component. Every color pair is hand-tuned in OKLCH to meet WCAG AA contrast requirements. Semantic HTML elements are used throughout — native dialog for modals, details for accordions, and proper ARIA attributes where needed.

mainEntity.name: How do Frutjam components compare to DaisyUI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both are CSS-only Tailwind CSS component libraries, but Frutjam is built specifically for Tailwind CSS v4, uses OKLCH color tokens with guaranteed WCAG AA contrast pairs, and ships a free MCP server (Cherry) for AI editor integration — DaisyUI's equivalent is paid. Frutjam also provides explicit on-{color} token pairs rather than computing foreground colors at runtime.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to install anything besides Tailwind CSS?

acceptedAnswer.text: Just one extra line. Add @plugin "frutjam"; to your CSS file after @import "tailwindcss"; and install via npm i -D frutjam. That's it — no PostCSS plugins, no JavaScript config, no separate stylesheet to import.

mainEntity.name: Can I use Frutjam components with React or Next.js?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Since Frutjam is CSS-only, you use components the same way in any stack — just apply the class names. For components that benefit from JavaScript control, Frutjam ships optional React hooks (frutjam/react) that wrap native DOM calls with no extra dependencies.
